newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields fall in line with foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields fall in line with foreigners.

text.p: Swedish debt yields fell in early trade Wednesday, mostly following the trend in foreign markets and with most of the focus on a further flattening of the yield curve.

"Its nothing but curve trading today and I think it will continue," said one dealer, adding that the market seemed to target 100 basis points between three and 10-year bonds. The spread currently stands at 115.
Six-month T-bills edged down one basis point to 4.28 percent and 10-year bond yields were down four basis points to 6.40 percent.
The solid interest in longer maturities also raised hopes for good bidding in today's two billion crown auction in the 10-year issue at 1050 GMT.
"Yields are at a very low level but the hunt for long bonds makes us believe in a good auction result," said one dealer.
The crown lost some ground and was trading at 4.3380 to the mark compared to 4.3220 late Tuesday.

"We saw a big order to sell crowns against the mark from a London player which pushed the mark up to 4.34 crown but I think we will calm down, unless we break 4.3460 crowns," said one dealer. -- Erik Aronsson, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1010
